introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2024. Additional Mathematics 2 (code 0575), Paper 2. Duration: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions, questions 1 to 8). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions, questions 9 to 11; if this section is chosen, Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (answer any two questions, questions 12 to 14; if this section is chosen, Section B may not be chosen). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.
incertitudes: Regles de choix : la consigne imprimee est « Section A obligatoire, puis DEUX questions de la Section B OU DEUX de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois ». Le systeme ne sait exprimer que « 2 parmi 3 » par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, pas de total par question. Le champ points de chaque exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions (Section A : 8 ou 9 ; Sections B et C : 17, ce qui est coherent avec « all questions carry equal marks » ; total 66 + 17 + 17 = 100).
Le sujet est une photo numerisee (CamScanner) : texte lu en image page par page ; les filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ont ete ignores.

questions.enonce_markdown: 1. (i) Find the value(s) of $x$ for which $(\log_3 x)^2-4(\log_3 x)+3=0$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Put $u=\log_3 x$. The equation becomes a quadratic in $u$:

$$u^2-4u+3=0.$$

Factorise: $(u-1)(u-3)=0$, so $u=1$ or $u=3$.

Go back to $x$:

- $\log_3 x=1$ gives $x=3^1=3$;
- $\log_3 x=3$ gives $x=3^3=27$.

Check: for $x=3$, $1-4+3=0$; for $x=27$, $9-12+3=0$.

**Answer: $x=3$ or $x=27$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) Given that the roots of the quadratic equation $2x^2-3x-5=0$ are $\alpha$ and $\beta$:

a) find the values of $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha\beta$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $ax^2+bx+c=0$ the sum of the roots is $-\dfrac{b}{a}$ and the product is $\dfrac{c}{a}$. Here $a=2$, $b=-3$, $c=-5$.

$\alpha+\beta=-\dfrac{-3}{2}=\dfrac32$ and $\alpha\beta=\dfrac{-5}{2}=-\dfrac52$.

**Answer: $\alpha+\beta=\dfrac32$ and $\alpha\beta=-\dfrac52$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) Write down another quadratic equation with integral coefficients whose roots are $-\alpha$ and $-\beta$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For the new roots $-\alpha$ and $-\beta$:

- sum $=-\alpha-\beta=-(\alpha+\beta)=-\dfrac32$;
- product $=(-\alpha)(-\beta)=\alpha\beta=-\dfrac52$.

A quadratic with sum $S$ and product $P$ of roots is $x^2-Sx+P=0$, so

$$x^2+\frac32x-\frac52=0.$$

Multiply by $2$ to get integral coefficients:

$$2x^2+3x-5=0.$$

Check: $2x^2-3x-5=(2x-5)(x+1)$ has roots $\frac52$ and $-1$; the new roots are $-\frac52$ and $1$, and $2x^2+3x-5=(2x+5)(x-1)$ has exactly these roots.

**Answer: $2x^2+3x-5=0$.**
